p.l: SUBHUMANS
Death to the Sickoids/Oh Canaduh
Crass Productions
no label
I like these guys. The A-side is
good (although I confess I'm not
really sure what Sickoids are), with nice
harmonies. The vocals are good, it's
hard to find a good male voice in
Canaduh. I think this band has
potential not fully realized!
While the mix on side two is lousy,
the pace is fast and the music is
strong. Nice drumming and guitar work,
but where is the bass? I think this
deserves to be the A-side. It's a
great song which could make an anthem
for stepped-on Canadians. I can hear
Margaret Trudeau humming it now......
"Don't have a job/Can't pay the rent/
And now we're paying interest on the
money we've been lent………"
DOA
The Prisoner/Thirteen
Quintessence Records
1869 W. 4th Ave
Vancouver, Canaduh V6J 1M4
One of 2 records on this new label
Music from the north. What can I say
about DOA? Everybody seems to like
them. I have a hard time getting
past the vocals. Joey Shithead cannot
sing. He cannot even get by with
what he does. It's too bad, because
the band is good and the music fast.
But what the hell is he saying? If
it's not important enough to hear,
why say it at all? All I could pick out
was: "Is everybody a bunch of wimps?"
I dunno, Joey. Are you?

div.p: The second side suffers from the same problems: lousy vocals. But the drumming of Chuck Biscuits carried the tune along. The only understandable line here is: "I'm one big zero." I think he hit it right on the head.

p.l: THE SHIRKERS
Drunk & Disorderly/Suicide
Limp Records
Rockville Pike
Rockville, Maryland 20852
I knew the singer Steve Bailer when
I lived in D.C. I always thought he
was devo, even before I had ever
heard of the band. So, I just to get his
record… I never would have thought
he'd do it. On the whole it's a bit of
a disappointment. Too much rock and
roll. It's got a good beat, but the
overall impact is too soft. I must say
I am surprised at how good Steve can
sing. Really. I like the female voice
on the chorus, it's a nice change. The
music is simple. A make-your-own-
record-be-a-star project. Capitol city
punk without the Capitol city anger.
POINTED STICKS
What Do You Want Me To Do/
Somebody's Mom
Quintessence Records
Finally, a great male Canadian
singer. It's about time. A perfect pop
voice. This is pop! A fun, jumping
song! a little boy’s plea with a great
beat. This is a tight band all around.
The harmonies are good, the hooks are
good, and above all the sound is good.
A new label with distinction. I think
this first song should be on the
radio. Pointed Sticks are like the Bay
City Rollers with more integrity.
A fine debut single from a band worth
checking out. You won't be sorry.
LEWD
Kill Yourself/Trashcan Babies/
Pay or Die
Scratch Records
2420 1st Ave
Seattle, Wash. 98121
A Clash-like opening. Enemy-like
vocals. Can't these guys be original?
I guess not. Boring old Satz. I mean,
like wow, man this is PUNK! My first
question: Why don't You kill yourself
Your music is as repetitive as disco.
The second song is a horror. I hate
it. Vocal retchings, sexist bullshit.
Give up.
The third song. My record player
kept rejecting it.
My second question. Do record
players have their own tastes in music?
POLY: In the new wave I only like the
Pistols, apart from us. And Reggae. I
was brought up on Reggae 'cause I
came from Brixton.
NEVA: Why do you think Reggae has
become so popular with punks?
POLY: Well, I like Reggae anyway
‘cause I'm half black, and I grew up in a
black area and was brought up on it...
So I can’t judge it by what other
punks say in any case. But punk and
Reggae are the same in the sense that
they're basic...Reggae is a very
basic music, it's not very technical, the
rhythm rules it. It's got its own
little language, its own little scene...
But it's changed a lot from Ska and
Blue Beat, now it's got heavily into
Dub and Rastafarian influences. It’s
more cultural. There's a lot of fakes
in it too, ‘cause if you're a real
Rasta you're not meant to show your
locks, you keep them under a hat
unless you're praying.
NEVA: How old were you when you left
home?
POLY: Fifteen. I just moved around for
a year, mostly living in squats. I
stayed with junkies for a little
while. I didn't really like it very much
but I didn't have nowhere else to
live. There's no flats available for
young single people, it's one of the
worst problems in London. It's
virtually impossible to get somewhere to
live, it really is, unless you've got
a load of money. These council flats
won't let single people in.
NEVA: Why do the papers over here make
such a big deal over everything the
punks do?
POLY: You know what the English are
like! It was just because it was new
and exciting that they had to blow it
up out of proportion. And it was
funny as well, that thing on "Today"-
(when the Pistols swore). It brought
the fun back into telly, that, and it
made the Pistols bloody famous!
NEVA: It sure did. Any last words, Poly?
POLY: Yeah. Do you want a cup of coffee?
